transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Turner: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, I have Miguel from our security/infra team. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Jill Park: Jill here, head of IT at Acme HealthTech, we also have Ravi and Aisha.
[00:12] Miguel Alvarez: Hey all. We'll try to keep this focused on SSO and RBAC mapping and then open to questions on audit logs and KMS.
[00:22] Ravi Singh: Great, our IdP is Okta, SCIM available, SAML 2.0, need to understand attributes and group sync. Also curious about service accounts and least privilege for our platform engineers.
[00:36] Sophie Turner: Perfect. On Redwood side we support SAML SSO with SP-initiated flow, ACS endpoint and SP metadata we provide. SCIM for provisioning and group sync — we map groups to roles. Quick note, we also can do Just-in-time provisioning but for enterprise customers we recommend SCIM for group memberships.
[00:54] Aisha Khan: When you say map groups to roles, what are the role primitives? Admin/developer/viewer? Can we create custom roles?
[01:05] Miguel Alvarez: Core roles are Admin, Developer, Viewer; Admin has billing and workspace policy controls, Developer can manage models and deployments, Viewer is read-only. We also support role scoping per workspace and custom role table via request — there is a process to add custom roles but not self-serve in the console today.
[01:27] Jill Park: For compliance we need least-privilege enforced via groups from Okta. Also SSO session timeout and 2FA enforcement — can we honor IdP policies?
[01:38] Sophie Turner: Yes, we honor SAML assertions for session creation and we can pass-through session length; we also support enforcing SSO-only login for orgs and can require MFA via IdP.
[01:48] Ravi Singh: On SCIM attributes — can you confirm the attribute schema? We need email, displayName, groups, and manager fields if possible for RBAC inheritance.
[01:58] Miguel Alvarez: Our SCIM implementation uses standard urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User attributes: userName (email), name.familyName/givenName, displayName, active, and groupMembership via /Groups endpoint. Manager attribute sometimes mapped to 'entitlements' but we can discuss custom mapping. We'll send the SCIM payload example.
[02:20] Aisha Khan: How do you handle group deletions and orphaned accounts?
[02:25] Sophie Turner: SCIM delta sync handles removes; if a user is removed from a group that maps to a role, RBAC updates in near real-time (within a minute or two depending on sync). For SAML-only orgs without SCIM we recommend short session TTL and manual offboarding.
[02:39] Ravi Singh: Service accounts — our CI/CD pipelines need programmatic access to Redwood endpoints. We can't tie those to human SSO. Best practice?
[02:48] Miguel Alvarez: Use scoped API keys or service principals. We offer long-lived API keys for service accounts but strongly recommend using short-lived tokens via our internal token exchange or integrating with external KMS/HSM for storing secrets. For highest compliance, pair service accounts with dedicated workspace and minimal roles.
[03:08] Jill Park: We need audit logs for all admin activity, ideally exported to our SIEM (Splunk). How granular are your logs and retention?
[03:17] Sophie Turner: We capture audit trails for auth events, role changes, model deployments, config changes. For Redwood Hosted we retain admin-level audit logs for 90 days by default, longer retention available as an add-on. We can push logs to customer S3 or syslog/HTTP endpoint; Splunk forwarder works fine. For Private deployments you control retention.
[03:39] Ravi Singh: Encryption — at rest encryption details and KMS support? We use a customer-managed key for PHI workloads.
[03:47] Miguel Alvarez: We encrypt at rest by default with provider-managed keys. We support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS and Cloud HSM) for Private deployments and Dedicated customers; for Hosted we can enable CMEK for enterprise contracts. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: Data residency — we need our data kept in us-west-2. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[04:12] Sophie Turner: Yes, we have region pinning for Dedicated and Private; Hosted customers can choose region where tenant is provisioned. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:21] Jill Park: SOC 2 and ISO, do you have reports and can they be shared under NDA?
[04:26] Sophie Turner: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we'll share redacted reports via our security portal and can produce an NDA'd bundle.
[04:34] Ravi Singh: One last thing — SCIM group-to-role mapping examples? We need to see a sample table with Okta group name => Redwood role mapping.
[04:42] Miguel Alvarez: We'll provide a mapping template. Example: okta_group: \"acme-admins\" => Redwood role: Admin; \"acme-platform\" => Developer. And we support multi-group mapping if you need role union semantics.
[04:56] Aisha Khan: Is there a way to limit access to model weights or specific endpoints for certain roles?
[05:02] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, model-level permissions can be scoped per workspace or per-route; you can lock model downloads and disallow weight export in Private deployments.
[05:12] Jill Park: PRocedural question: When we onboard, what's the recommended sequence?
[05:16] Sophie Turner: 1) Redwood provides SAML metadata + SCIM endpoints and RBAC template; 2) Customer IdP team does test SSO and SCIM provisioning in staging; 3) Validate roles and do smoke tests; 4) Cutover and enable enforcement and longer audit retention if needed.
[05:31] Ravi Singh: Ok makes sense. We'll coordinate IdP people.
[05:34] Sophie Turner: Great. Any open security objections I should note?
[05:38] Jill Park: Mostly about CMEK and log forwarding SLA. Also want to confirm retention for audit logs beyond 90 days for SOC2.
[05:48] Miguel Alvarez: We have add-on for 365/730 day retention and can set up an export to your S3. SLA for log delivery in enterprise contract.
[05:56] Sophie Turner: I'll follow up with the docs and mapping templates, set up the IdP test. Thanks everyone.
[05:59] Aisha Khan: Thanks all.
[05:60] End of recording
notes: Customer prefers SCIM-based provisioning and Okta integration. They require CMEK for PHI and log forwarding to Splunk. Action: schedule IdP test next week.
